title: Ayurvedic Panchakarma Detoxification Therapy

faqs.question: Will I receive all five Panchakarma procedures?
faqs.draftAnswer: The procedures discussed under Panchakarma are not a checklist you should assume will all be performed. Ask which procedures are proposed for you, why, and what alternatives are available before agreeing to a treatment plan.
faqs.reviewRequired: Confirm procedures actually offered, selection and consent criteria, and whether blood-letting/leech therapy is provided.

faqs.question: How do I know whether this programme is suitable for me?
faqs.draftAnswer: Explain your diagnosis, current symptoms and goals before booking. In particular, discuss heart or kidney disease, pregnancy, recent surgery and previous reactions to cleansing procedures. Ask whether this programme is appropriate and whether another form of care is needed first.
faqs.reviewRequired: Confirm eligibility, exclusions, reports required and how suitability is assessed before payment/travel.

faqs.question: Can I continue my prescribed medicines?
faqs.draftAnswer: Do not stop or change prescribed medicines on your own. Share a complete list of medicines and supplements with your treating clinicians and discuss any proposed Ayurvedic medicines with them.
faqs.reviewRequired: Confirm interaction review, prescribing responsibility, communication with existing clinicians and programme-specific restrictions.

faqs.question: What risks or side effects should I discuss before treatment?
faqs.draftAnswer: Ask the physician to explain the risks and alternatives for each proposed procedure or medicine in relation to your health. Raise any new symptoms promptly and ask what help is available if you become unwell.
faqs.reviewRequired: Provide specific common/serious risks, contraindications, monitoring, escalation and actual out-of-hours arrangements. Do not publish a zero-risk claim.

faqs.question: What results can I realistically expect, and how long should I stay?
faqs.draftAnswer: Results and suitable duration vary. Discuss achievable goals and how progress would be reviewed before booking. A stated minimum stay is a booking condition, not a promise of improvement within that time.
faqs.reviewRequired: Confirm programme-specific goals and duration; substantiate or remove existing outcome percentages and cure/permanence claims.

faqs.question: Can a companion stay with me?
faqs.draftAnswer: Non-participating companions are considered case by case. Tell the team about your accommodation and assistance needs before booking, and ask for confirmation of availability, responsibilities and charges.
faqs.reviewRequired: Owner-approved case-by-case principle from 7 September; business owner must confirm rates/inclusions, clinical team must confirm care duties and dependency limits.

faqs.question: What follow-up should I arrange after returning home?
faqs.draftAnswer: Before leaving, ask what advice you should take home, who to contact with questions and how ongoing care should be coordinated with your usual clinician. Confirm any follow-up appointments and charges before agreeing to them.
faqs.reviewRequired: Confirm actual discharge documentation, clinician availability, cadence, channel, charges and medicine supply/export arrangements.

researchQuestions.question: Which of the five procedures will I actually have: all of them, including induced vomiting, purgation, medicated enemas and Raktamokshana (blood-letting), or only the ones my physician chooses?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The Process section presents all five as "the following steps" of the programme. A 60-year-old reading "controlled emesis" and an unexplained "Raktamokshana" assumes the worst and does not book.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner: Dr. Deepu John to state which procedures KTAHV performs, how they are selected, and whether blood-letting or leech therapy is offered

researchQuestions.question: I take blood-pressure, diabetes, thyroid, statin or blood-thinner medication. Can I keep taking it through the purgation and emesis days, and who adjusts my doses?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Emesis and purgation cause fluid and electrolyte shifts and can change how pills are absorbed. The page's own testimonial suggests stopping medicines, which frightens careful patients and their GPs.
researchQuestions.answerSource: The principle is on /online-consultation/ ("never stop a prescribed medicine without their guidance"). The Panchakarma-specific protocol needs physician/owner. The medication FAQ on /personalized-customized-healing-program/ needs physician verification before reuse.

researchQuestions.question: Am I too old or too unwell for Panchakarma? Who should not have it (heart disease, pacemaker, kidney disease, osteoporosis, recent surgery, cancer treatment, pregnancy)?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: FAQ 3 says it suits "the majority of people" but never names who is excluded. A patient over 60 with other conditions needs to know before paying for flights.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (no stated maximum age; senior-patient considerations). The contraindication list itself needs physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: I pay 100% in advance and fly in. If the physician then decides Panchakarma is not right for me, do I get a refund, a switch to a gentler programme, or nothing?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page requires full prepayment and gives no refund within 15 days of arrival. /cancellation-and-refund-policy/ gives no refund for early departure. This is the biggest financial fear for an older international patient.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner (policy). Partial: /cancellation-and-refund-policy/ allows medical-emergency exceptions with management approval, and the free pre-screen on /online-consultation/ lowers the risk.

researchQuestions.question: How many nights do I need (7, 14 or 21), and what is the realistic total cost including the procedures, medicines and tests?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page gives 7–21 days in the FAQ and 14 nights minimum elsewhere, prices per villa per night, and even lists Panchakarma as an add-on. The patient cannot budget.
researchQuestions.answerSource: This page (villa rates, 14-night minimum) and /faqs-downloads/ (Panchakarma from 14 nights). Whether the procedures are included, and an indicative cost for medicines and tests, needs physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: What is a main-procedure day really like? How long do the vomiting or purgation last, am I confined to my villa, is a nurse or doctor with me, and is there a private toilet?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The only daily routine shown is a generic wellness day (06:30 yoga, 11:00 nature walk), which cannot be true on emesis or purgation days. The unknown is what stops people booking.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner. The attached bathroom per villa is stated on /faqs-downloads/.

researchQuestions.question: What side effects might I have (weakness, dehydration, dizziness, headache), and how are they managed?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page claims "Zero adverse reactions" while /faqs-downloads/ admits mild detoxification symptoms. The contradiction destroys trust. An honest answer builds it.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ ("Will I experience any side effects during treatment?"). Procedure-specific risks and how they are managed need physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: If I become seriously unwell (chest pain, severe dehydration, low blood sugar), is a doctor on campus at night, and how far is the nearest emergency hospital?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Patients aged 40–70 with other conditions are travelling to rural Palakkad. Emergency cover decides the booking for them and their families.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (arrangements with nearby hospitals, 24-hour assistance, emergency services on call, advice to buy evacuation insurance). Night doctor or nurse cover and the nearest hospital's name and distance need physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: Who will my physician be, what are their qualifications, will the same doctor see me throughout, and do they speak my language (German, French, Russian, Arabic)?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page says "Doctor might change as subject to availability" and mentions "multilingual staff" without naming a language. Continuity and language matter most on emesis and enema days.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /online-consultation/ (Dr. Deepu John, Chief Physician & Head of Department, BAMS, 12+ years, helped draft the NABH Panchakarma Clinic Standards; Dr. Akhila Oommen and Dr. Rahul R, BAMS). Languages and continuity need physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: When will I feel results and how long do they last? Will I feel worse before I feel better?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page's only answer is the unsourced "87% within two weeks / 94% long-term". Many people feel tired for days after the procedures, and a patient needs to plan work and travel around that.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner (the page's statistics must not be reused)

researchQuestions.question: Do I need blood tests or reports before I come, and will you run tests on arrival? At what cost?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page says "Bring ... recent reports" and that lab tests cost extra, but not which tests or how much. Older patients often have recent bloodwork they can bring.
researchQuestions.answerSource: This page (bring reports; tests extra) and /online-consultation/ (health-summary step, reports optional). Which tests and what they cost need physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: What will I eat? Will I fast, drink medicated ghee or eat only kitchari? Can you handle diabetes, gluten or lactose intolerance? With coffee banned, how do I cope with caffeine withdrawal?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Diet on procedure days differs from the "three organic, sattvic meals" described. Ghee intake worries people with high cholesterol or diabetes, and caffeine withdrawal causes headaches.
researchQuestions.answerSource: This page (vegetarian or vegan meals, coffee abstinence) and /faqs-downloads/ (dietary restrictions and allergies; caffeine-free campus). The procedure-phase diet and any internal oleation need physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: How soon after my last procedure can I take a long-haul flight, and what must I avoid for the first weeks at home?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The flight home is booked before arrival. Post-procedure recovery rules decide the departure date and the length of the stay.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner

researchQuestions.question: What follow-up do I get once I'm home: online reviews, medicines shipped abroad, a discharge summary for my own doctor? What does it cost?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page only says "Continuous post-discharge wellness plan". Patients abroad need to know their GP will get documents and that they can get medicines.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (online follow-ups at 1, 3 and 6 months; admission and discharge notes; pharmacy supply to take home). Follow-up cost and international shipping or customs need physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: Which visa do I need (e-Visa, Medical Visa, Medical Attendant Visa for my spouse), and will you send an invitation letter?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: A stay of at least 14 nights for treatment raises the question of whether a tourist e-Visa is appropriate.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (visa FAQ and invitation letter on request) and /how-to-reach/ (visa and entry, official portal link)

researchQuestions.question: Is the airport transfer included, which airport should I fly into, and can someone meet me late at night?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: This page lists transfers under Inclusions, but /faqs-downloads/ charges for them. Older travellers need door-to-door certainty.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (Coimbatore 75 km, about 2 hours; transfer ₹6,775 MPV one way; book 48 hours ahead) and /how-to-reach/. The included-or-extra conflict needs physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: Can my spouse come without having Panchakarma, what do they pay, and can they follow a lighter programme?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Patients aged 40–70 rarely travel alone for 2–3 weeks.
researchQuestions.answerSource: This page (add-ons: extra bed ₹3,000 / €38 / $43; extra meals ₹5,500 / €69 / $79) and /faqs-downloads/ (companion FAQ; two people on different programmes)

researchQuestions.question: What happens if Panchakarma doesn't help my complaint? Is there a review, an extension or any credit?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page's promises ("permanently resolving disease") raise expectations. An honest answer about what happens if it doesn't work lowers the perceived risk.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner

researchQuestions.question: Is this a hospital or a spa? Will my insurer reimburse it, and will you issue admission and discharge papers?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The same page lists "Spa", "Luxury Hotel" and "Resort" awards and a "Book Your Stay" button. Insurers and employers reject holiday invoices.
researchQuestions.answerSource: This page (NABH certificate AH-2024-0250, valid to 24 April 2027), /faqs-downloads/ (no cashless cover; reimbursement documents) and /online-consultation/ ("a medical institution, not a leisure property")

researchQuestions.question: I have knee or hip arthritis. Can I safely get on and off an oily treatment table, are the floors slippery, are there steps to my villa, and is a wheelchair available?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Oil therapies plus limited mobility means a fall risk, which is a specific worry for this age group and for the "chronic joint problems" patients the page targets.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (senior-patient considerations, ramps) and /how-to-reach/ (wheelchair-accessible vehicle, caregiver). Treatment-room and villa access details need physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: Will my therapist be the same gender as me, and are enemas and emesis done privately and with dignity?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: This decides the booking for many Middle East patients and for many older European patients facing intimate procedures.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner

researchQuestions.question: What is the best season for Panchakarma, and can I cope with the monsoon or summer heat at my age?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Timing a trip of at least 14 nights around the climate and the traditional Panchakarma season.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (climate by season; monsoon traditionally best for intensive Panchakarma)

researchQuestions.question: Where do your statistics (80%, 87%, 94%, 92%, 30,000+, 100,000+) come from?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Well-read international patients distrust unsourced percentages, and unsourced numbers make the rest of the page look like marketing.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner (provide the source or remove)

researchQuestions.question: Can I stay connected: Wi-Fi in my villa, mobile signal?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Patients aged 40–70 often still work or look after family. This page charges for internet while /faqs-downloads/ says Wi-Fi in common areas is free.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (Wi-Fi in common areas; ask about in-villa). The conflict needs physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: I take metformin or insulin, blood-pressure tablets, a statin, thyroxine, or a GLP-1 injection (Ozempic/Wegovy/Mounjaro). Do I keep taking them, and can your herbs or the diet interact or cause low blood sugar?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Most 40–70-year-olds with obesity take at least one of these. The page lists diabetes as a target group and says 'Bring: medications' but never says what happens to them. The sitewide question 'Can I continue my current (allopathic) medicines during treatment?' has an empty answer.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner (Dr. Deepu John)

researchQuestions.question: Who should not come? Is there a BMI, weight or age limit, and can I come with heart disease, uncontrolled diabetes or hypertension, sleep apnoea (CPAP), kidney or liver disease, or after bariatric surgery?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Patients with comorbidities fear being turned away on arrival or being harmed. The page lists only who the programme is FOR. The sitewide 'Which conditions do you NOT treat?' is blank.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner; /faqs-downloads/ covers age only (18+, no stated maximum)

researchQuestions.question: How much weight can someone like me realistically lose in 14, 21 or 28 nights, and how is progress measured (weight, waist, BMI, blood sugar, lipids)?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The only numbers on the page are testimonials (4 kg in 7 days, 70 kg) and an unsourced '87%'. A patient paying for a long-haul flight needs an honest expected range and a clear measure of success.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner

researchQuestions.question: Will I regain the weight once I am home?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Regain is the main fear of anyone who has dieted before. The '94% sustain results after 6 months' claim is unsourced, and the FAQ covers follow-up logistics but not maintenance.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner (evidence behind any figure)

researchQuestions.question: What will the total bill be for 14 nights, including internal medicines and lab tests?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page says 'All-Inclusive... No hidden fees!' and also says medicines and tests 'can only be ascertained as your treatment progresses and will cost extra'. An international patient cannot budget without a typical range.
researchQuestions.answerSource: per-night rates are on this page (× 14 nights); the typical medicine and lab cost range needs owner

researchQuestions.question: Who will my physician be, what are their qualifications, and do they speak my language (German, French, Russian, Arabic)?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: This page names no physician. 'Multilingual staff' does not say which languages, and Process step 07 promises a 'Private Doctor' while another line says 'Doctor might change'.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /online-consultation/ (panel: Dr. Deepu John, Chief Physician & Head of Department, BAMS; Dr. Akhila Oommen, BAMS; Dr. Rahul R, BAMS). Languages need owner; the sitewide language FAQ is blank.

researchQuestions.question: If my blood sugar drops, my blood pressure spikes or I get chest pain, is a doctor on site at night, and how far is the nearest allopathic hospital?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Older patients with diabetes or cardiac risk who change diet and add herbs worry about emergencies in a rural location. The page is silent on this.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ in part (arrangements with nearby hospitals; emergency services on call for senior patients). Night/weekend doctor cover and the named nearest hospital and its distance need owner.

researchQuestions.question: Can my body size and mobility cope: getting on and off the wooden treatment table, the herbal steam box, stairs, bathrooms, walking distances on a 65-acre campus?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: This is specific to obesity. The page pictures Udwarthanam on a table and Bashpa Swedana in a wooden steam cabinet but says nothing about weight capacity, accessibility or knee and joint limits.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ in part (senior considerations: ramps, mobility assistance). Table and steam-box capacity and villa accessibility need owner.

researchQuestions.question: Will I be hungry? Is there enough protein on a vegetarian menu, can you cater for gluten or lactose intolerance, and is the diet safe for a diabetic?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The FAQ says there is no strict diet while the About section says 'structured personalized vegetarian diet'. Western patients used to meat-based protein want to know how the menu works and whether it is safe with their medication.

researchQuestions.question: Is Panchakarma (e.g. purgation or enemas) part of the weight programme, is it safe at my age, and does it cost extra?

researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner (clinical suitability and price)

researchQuestions.question: Which blood tests or reports should I send before booking, and are tests done on admission?

researchQuestions.question: What if I do not lose weight or my blood results do not improve? Is there any refund or follow-up plan?

'Relief from obesity, diabetes, and metabolic sluggishness' and 'Improved cardiac health, energy, and sleep quality'. These are disease and cardiovascular claims.
'Holistic and gentle weight loss with no harsh side effects' and 'Sustainable weight reduction via natural and herbal remedies'. These are absolute safety and outcome claims.
'Kairali’s program enables you to achieve sustainable weight loss and a healthier life'. This is an outcome promise.
FAQ: 'Most guests feel noticeable changes—better digestion, increased energy, and weight shifts—within 1–2 weeks'. This is an outcome and time-frame claim.
Detox claims: FAQ 'eliminate toxins' and 'assessing ... toxin levels', hero 'body detox', routine 'detoxifying drink to kickstart the metabolism', and Udwarthana 'to promote detoxification'.

FAQ: 'The plan includes Panchakarma detox'. The physician must decide whether Panchakarma is part of the weight protocol and whether it suits older or comorbid patients. The page elsewhere calls it a charged add-on.
FAQ: 'Do I need to follow a strict diet? No.' The diet is prescribed, and this matters for patients with diabetes on glucose-lowering drugs.

'Who is This Program For?' lists 'Those with diabetes' and 'Desire for healthy cardiac function and lower risk factors' without any medication or contraindication guidance. The physician must define eligibility and exclusions.

Testimonials and headings: 'losing 70kg', 'overcoming depression' (a mental-health outcome), 'shed 4kg in just 7 days ... quick and healthy results', the 'OVER 100 INCHES FROM MY BODY' thumbnail, and 'Transformative Results'. These need patient consent, substantiation and an 'individual results vary' line.
'Personalized Internal Medicines: Only physician-prescribed, in-house remedies (GMP-certified) for safe, targeted care'. This is a safety claim about the medicines.

'Clinical Excellence: Led by 5th-generation Ayurvedic physicians, each treatment is reviewed for maximum safety and efficacy'. This is an efficacy claim, and the generation count conflicts with 'four generations' elsewhere.

FAQ follow-up protocol: 'monthly virtual check-in for the first 3 months, then quarterly, to ensure ... results are long-lasting' conflicts with /faqs-downloads/ '1, 3 and 6 months'. The physician must set one schedule and drop the guarantee.

FAQ: 'You can order prescribed Ayurvedic supplements and herbal formulations ... delivery to most locations worldwide'. This means continuing prescribed medicines abroad without a local doctor, and cross-border import legality is unconfirmed.
Process step 02 ('body-mind imbalances caused by stress or high work demands') is copied from a stress programme. The physician should write the actual weight-management assessment.

Missing and needs physician authorship before go-live: guidance on continuing allopathic medicines (especially insulin, sulfonylureas, GLP-1 agonists and antihypertensives), contraindications and BMI/comorbidity limits, and the realistic expected-results statement.

researchQuestions.question: I take blood-pressure, cholesterol, diabetes, thyroid, antidepressant or blood-thinning medicine. Do I keep taking it, and can your herbal medicines interact with it?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Almost every 40–70-year-old burnout or lifestyle patient is on at least one of these. The page only says "Bring: ... medications" and never says whether they will be told to stop anything. Fear of interactions is the top reason a doctor at home advises against booking.

researchQuestions.question: I'm 64 with hypertension, a heart stent or type 2 diabetes. Are daily herbal steam baths, long oil therapies and the detox diet safe for me? Who should NOT do this programme?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The inclusions promise "herbal steam baths" daily and "detoxification". Older patients with cardiac or metabolic conditions worry about heat, dehydration and blood-sugar swings, and the page gives no contraindications or age guidance.
researchQuestions.answerSource: Needs physician: contraindications and how therapies are modified for age and comorbidity. FAQs & Downloads confirms there is no maximum age, which can be reused.

researchQuestions.question: What does "detoxification" actually involve here: only massages and steam, or Panchakarma procedures such as purgation, enemas or drinking medicated ghee?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page is labelled "Shodhanam Karma" (purification) yet lists Panchakarma as a paid add-on. FAQs & Downloads puts "Panchakarma & Detoxification" at 14+ nights. A patient cannot tell what their body will go through, which matters with high cholesterol, diabetes or a sensitive gut.
researchQuestions.answerSource: Needs physician: a plain list of the procedures in this programme versus the separate Panchakarma programme (/panchakarma-therapy/).

researchQuestions.question: Should I choose this programme, the Ayurvedic Panchakarma Detoxification programme, the Preventive Health & Regenerative programme or a stress programme?

A patient paying for long-haul travel fears picking the wrong one.
researchQuestions.answerSource: Other site pages (Panchakarma, Preventive & Regenerative, stress/sleep programmes) plus a physician-approved comparison line. The free online consultation (/online-consultation/) is the honest routing answer.

researchQuestions.question: Who exactly will be my doctor? What are their qualifications and experience, and will they speak my language (English, German, French, Russian, Arabic)?

researchQuestions.question: If I have a medical emergency (chest pain, a fall, a severe reaction), is there a doctor on site at night, and how far is the nearest modern hospital?

researchQuestions.question: Will I feel worse before I feel better? What side effects are normal during detox?

existingClinicalFlags: "87% symptom reduction within 14 days, 94% maintain improvements after 6 months" (Why Choose). An outcome statistic with no study, sample or method. It also measures at 14 days while the package minimum is 7 nights. Evidence or removal needed.

"Zero adverse reactions in 100,000+ therapies" (Why Choose). An absolute safety claim that contradicts the site's own FAQs & Downloads, which reports mild headaches, fatigue and digestive changes during detox.
"92% patient satisfaction from international guests (2024 data)" and "Trusted by 80% of guests". Survey figures with no source. The owner must supply the data, or the claims come out.
"Effective Relief from Chronic & Lifestyle Disorders" and "Relief from chronic conditions such as digestive disorders, fatigue, and metabolic imbalances". Efficacy claims for disease categories.

"Restoration of hormonal balance, reduction of inflammation, and alleviation of stress-related symptoms" and "Hormonal balance, stress reduction, and enhanced mental clarity". Physiological outcome claims.
"Strengthening of immunity and enhancement of metabolic and digestive functions". An immunity claim.

FAQ: "Can the treatment help with my chronic health conditions (like headaches, digestive problems, or back pain)? Yes. Our approach uniquely addresses..." An unconditional yes before assessment, plus a superiority claim. It conflicts with the Disclaimer page ("does not diagnose or cure medical issues").

FAQ: "Absolutely. This program is specifically designed for... burnout, sleep disruption, fatigue... address these challenges at their root." Suitability promised before assessment, and "at their root" implies cause-level resolution.

FAQ: "For optimal, lasting results, 14–21 days are recommended... improvements in as little as 7 days." A duration and outcome promise that conflicts with the 7-night minimum and with FAQs & Downloads ("Panchakarma & Detoxification — from 14 nights").
The "Shodhanam Karma" label and "deep detoxification". The physician must confirm whether this programme includes any shodhana (purification) procedures, since the page sells Panchakarma separately.
Daily "herbal steam baths" (Inclusions) given to all patients with no stated contraindications. This is a safety issue for hypertensive, cardiac and elderly patients (the target 40–70 audience).
"Ongoing support ensures long-term health" (Post Treatment) and FAQ "follow-up consultations to ensure your results last". Guarantees of lasting outcome.
"Whether you’re seeking to... prevent health complications before they start". A disease-prevention claim.

"Clinical Excellence: Led by 5th-generation Ayurvedic physicians, each treatment is reviewed for maximum safety and efficacy". A superlative safety/efficacy claim, and a generation count that contradicts "four generations" elsewhere.
"Your assigned doctor is available for unlimited consultations. Medical support is on call 24/7." A clinical service-level commitment. Night medical cover must be confirmed before it is published.
"Comprehensive Health Assessment: Tailored consultation and advanced diagnostics". The physician must say which diagnostics are meant, since lab tests are charged extra.

"Personalized Internal Medicines: Only physician-prescribed, in-house remedies (GMP-certified)" and the FAQ price range "(₹5,000–15,000)". The certification scope and the price range need confirmation.

Testimonial outcome wording: "my energy levels are now fully restored, and I feel renewed from within" under the heading "Transformative Results", plus a testimonial by "Dr. Regina Joseph". The patient's consent and genuineness need checking, and an outcome testimonial needs clinical/legal review before it stays.

title: Diabetes & Metabolic Balance Therapy

existingClinicalFlags: FAQ 1: 'Can Ayurvedic treatment cure diabetes completely?' and 'a complete cure depends on various factors…' imply a full cure is achievable. Dr. Deepu John must rewrite this as management with no remission promise, and exclude type 1 explicitly.

FAQ 2: 'Yes, Ayurvedic treatment is generally safe for diabetic individuals.' This is a blanket safety claim. The physician must state the pre-admission checks (medicines, kidney function, hypoglycaemia risk) and the contraindications.

FAQ 4: 'which may lead to a reduction in the need for diabetes medications' is a claim about reducing or stopping medicine. The physician must define who adjusts insulin or oral drugs during and after admission, and say patients never change them on their own.
'has successfully treated over 10,000 diabetic patients' and 'With over a century of experience' are unsourced volume and outcome claims. They need hospital records or removal.
'Instead of merely symptom management, we target the root causes of diabetes' is a root-cause treatment claim.

'We choose herbs like bitter melon, fenugreek, and Indian gooseberry for their anti-diabetic properties, aiding blood sugar regulation and organ protection' is an efficacy and organ-protection claim. It also needs a hypoglycaemia and drug-interaction safety line for patients on insulin or sulfonylureas.
Process step 3: 'regulate blood sugar levels, enhance pancreatic function' is a claim about pancreatic function.

Process step 2: 'Virechana (therapeutic purgation) and Basti (medicated enema)' for diabetic patients. The physician must confirm suitability, fluid and glucose monitoring, and contraindications (on hypoglycaemic drugs, CKD, elderly). The physician must also confirm whether Panchakarma is part of this programme or a paid add-on.
'Two Ayurvedic therapies per day, including herbal steam baths': the physician must confirm heat and steam safety for patients with diabetic neuropathy, cardiac disease or foot problems.

'Why' bullets: 'Ayurvedic methods maintain stable blood sugar, reducing dangerous fluctuations', 'Enhanced Insulin Sensitivity: Improve insulin effectiveness', 'Hormonal Balance: Target underlying hormonal issues to restore equilibrium', 'Ayurveda alleviates common diabetes symptoms like thirst and fatigue'. All are outcome claims.
Benefits: 'Steadier blood sugar through detox therapies, herbal medication, and a personalized diet'. Yoga step: 'improve insulin sensitivity'.
'Diabetes is a lifestyle disease' is medically inaccurate for type 1. The physician must correct it to wording specific to type 2.

The suitability list ('Type 2 diabetic individuals', 'Pre-diabetic individuals', 'Individuals with insulin resistance') has no exclusions. The physician must supply who is NOT eligible; it must not be invented.

The testimonial ('helped naturally control my blood sugar levels', Ms. Rashi) under the H2 'Transformative Results' is an outcome testimonial on a YMYL page. It needs consent and authenticity checks and a statement that results vary.
Diet: the generic routine gives diabetic patients 'fresh juice', 'cooked oats with fruits' and 'freshly prepared juices… after every session'. The physician must approve a diabetes-appropriate menu.

Therapy list: 'massages like Thakaradhara, Pizhichil, and Abhyangam' against Process ('Abhyangam, Shirodhara, Udwarthanam'). The physician must confirm which therapies this programme uses and describe them correctly.
Hero and meta description: 'control sugar' and 'herbal meds' are a glycaemic-control claim in the search snippet.

'Our expert nutritionists provide personalized dietary recommendations to manage diabetes effectively' is a staffing and clinical-diet claim with no roster evidence. The owner and physician must confirm it.

existingClinicalFlags: Hero, meta description and og:description: 'Heal naturally from addiction ... Personalized therapies for lasting recovery'. This promises a permanent outcome.
FAQ 2: answers 'Yes' to 'Is the program suitable for all types of addictions?'. Which substances are accepted, and which patients are excluded, must be set by the physician.

'Who is This Program For? ... Those experiencing cravings, withdrawal, or relapse cycles' together with the terms line 'Abstinence from Smoking, Alcohol, & Coffee is strictly adhered to'. This implies acute alcohol, sedative or opioid withdrawal is managed on site. The page needs a withdrawal-safety protocol, night medical cover and an escalation hospital, or a statement that patients must be medically detoxed before admission.
FAQ 3: 'They address the root causes of addiction'. Unsupported mechanism and efficacy claim.
History section: 'Ayurvedic treatments excel in tackling drug and alcohol addictions', 'ensure enduring recovery', 'the proven effectiveness of Ayurvedic treatments'.
'Proven Effectiveness: ... effectively addressing addiction for lasting recovery'. No evidence or outcome data is cited.

Benefits: 'Reduced cravings, steadier energy, and sharper focus through herbal support'. States a clinical effect of herbs and says nothing about interactions with naltrexone, acamprosate, disulfiram, SSRIs or other psychiatric medicines, or about liver safety in alcohol-related liver disease.

Process step 02 and Benefits: Panchakarma 'eliminating accumulated toxins caused by substance abuse' / 'clears the toxins built up through substance use'. A mechanism claim. It also needs a statement on whether Panchakarma suits patients who are malnourished, elderly or have liver disease after long-term drinking.

The name 'Behavioral Health Therapy' and the promise of 'psychological therapies like individual and spiritual counselling'. The site names only BAMS physicians, so who delivers psychological care, and whether it is within scope of practice, must be confirmed.

Sanskrit name 'Madātyaya Chikitsa' applied to drug and tobacco dependence. Classically, madātyaya refers to alcohol-related disorder, so the physician should confirm the name is right for the whole programme.

Testimonials (Mr. Vivek, Mr. Kevin, Mr. Jaydon, each 5.0) make outcome claims: 'conventional therapies had not been effective', 'lowering cravings', 'helped me regain my life'. 'Families seeking a safe, supportive environment for a loved one’s recovery'. Consent and voluntary admission need a statement. Why section: 'We promote long-term, sustainable relief'. This is a durability claim with no evidence.

These need provenance (real patients, consent, dates) plus physician and legal sign-off before production.

Generic day plan used for this programme: Abhyanga/Udwarthana 'to promote detoxification', afternoon 'fresh juice', a 21:00 'warm herbal bath', 30–45 minutes of yoga at 06:30. The physician must confirm these suit sinus/migraine patients or label the plan as not programme-specific.

Title, meta and hero lede: 'Sinus & Migraine Ayurvedic Relief…' / 'Natural Ayurvedic sinusitis & migraine relief with herbal therapies, Nasyam & Shirodhara'. 'Relief' is a promise in the SERP snippet.

Missing safety content that must be written by Dr. Deepu John before any new FAQ ships: contraindications for Nasyam and Shirodhara, co-use with conventional migraine and sinus medication, managing acute attacks during the stay, recommended programme duration for this condition, realistic time to improvement, and a line that this programme does not replace the patient's neurologist or ENT, with urgent care for a sudden severe headache.

faqs.reviewRequired: Confirm actual discharge documentation, clinician availability, cadence, channel, charges and medicine supply/export arrangements.

researchQuestions.question: I take antidepressants, anti-anxiety medicine or sleeping pills (and/or blood-pressure drugs or blood thinners). Can I keep taking them, will your herbal medicines interact with them, and will you ask me to stop?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: This is the first question for most 40–70-year-old stress patients. The only FAQ answers it with 'natural sources, minimal side effects', which reads as evasive to a patient who has been warned about herb–drug interactions.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner (Dr. Deepu John). Partial: /online-consultation/ already says 'never stop a prescribed medicine without their guidance'.

researchQuestions.question: Is this programme for everyday stress, or also for diagnosed anxiety disorder, depression, burnout or panic attacks? Who is it NOT suitable for?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The hero says 'anxiety' and the H1 says 'Mental Wellness', but no exclusion criteria are given (severe depression, suicidal thoughts, psychosis, bipolar disorder). A careful patient or their family will not book without knowing scope and safety limits.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner

researchQuestions.question: Is a psychiatrist or psychologist on site or on call, and what happens if I have a panic attack or a mental-health crisis during my stay? How far is the nearest hospital?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Patients with anxiety fear being far from home without support. /faqs-downloads/ only mentions generic 'arrangements with nearby hospitals'.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner (named partner hospital, distance, psychiatric referral path). Partial: /faqs-downloads/ ('medical evacuation', 'emergency medical services on call').

researchQuestions.question: I also have high blood pressure, diabetes or a heart condition. Are Shirodhara, steam (Swedana) and oil therapies safe for me, and is there an upper age limit?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Stress often comes with hypertension and cardiac risk at 40–70. The page names steam and detox procedures but gives no contraindications.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (no stated maximum age; senior-patient considerations). Contraindications need physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: Which therapies will I actually get for stress each day? Is Shirodhara or a head therapy included in the two daily therapies, or is it extra?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The sample day is generic boilerplate (Udwarthana, one therapy slot) shared with 28 other pages. A patient cannot see what makes this a stress programme or what the fee buys.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner

researchQuestions.question: What will my total bill be? Are herbal medicines, lab tests and consultations included, and can I get an estimate before paying 100% in advance?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: On the same page, 'All-Inclusive / No hidden fees' contradicts 'Internal Medicines… will cost extra'. /faqs-downloads/ says medicines are included. With 100% advance payment and no refund inside 15 days, cost uncertainty stops the booking.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner (this page and /faqs-downloads/ contradict each other)

researchQuestions.question: Which rates apply if I come after 30 September 2026?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The rates on this page expire in 7 days. Other pages say 31 Oct 2026 or 1 Oct 2026 – 30 Sep 2027.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner

researchQuestions.question: How soon will I feel a difference, and is 7 nights enough or should I stay 14 or 21?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: International patients plan flights and leave around this. The page lists 7/14/21/28 days with no guidance on how to choose.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (stress relief: 7 nights minimum, duration set at consultation). Timing of benefit needs physician/owner (no outcome % may be invented).

researchQuestions.question: Who will my doctor be, what are their qualifications, and do they speak my language (German, French, Russian, Arabic)? Will the same doctor see me throughout?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Talking about stress and mental health needs a shared language and continuity. The page says 'Doctor might change as subject to availability' and claims 'multilingual staff' without naming any language.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /online-consultation/ and the home page (Dr. Deepu John, Chief Physician, BAMS; Dr. Rahul R, BAMS; Dr. Akhila Oommen, BAMS). Languages and continuity policy need physician/owner. /how-to-reach/ says 'our team communicates in English'.

researchQuestions.question: I mainly can't sleep, or I want something yoga-led. Should I choose this, Sleep Restoration Therapy, or the Yoga-Based Stress & Energy Reset, and why do they cost different amounts?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Three pages cover overlapping ground. Sleep Restoration also claims 'insomnia, anxiety & stress'. The yoga reset costs more (Maharaja Suite single ₹49,480 against ₹48,267 here). The page doesn't cross-link or compare them.
researchQuestions.answerSource: another site page: /sleep-restoration-therapy/ and /yoga-based-stress-energy-reset-program/. The distinction needs physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: Is this a medical hospital stay or a wellness holiday? Will I get admission and discharge documents my doctor and insurer at home will accept?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page is full of 'luxury', 'spa' and 'retreat' wording, which undercuts the hospital claim for a patient (and an insurer) deciding whether this is treatment.
researchQuestions.answerSource: another site page: /how-to-reach/ ('It is not a spa… NABH-accredited Ayurvedic hospital') and /faqs-downloads/ (admission and discharge notes, treatment summaries, reimbursement documents)

researchQuestions.question: What follow-up do I get after I go home? Can you send a discharge summary to my psychiatrist or GP, and can I take or ship my herbal medicines home through customs?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Stress relapses after return to work. The page says 'Continuous post-discharge wellness plan' without saying what it contains.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (online follow-ups at 1, 3 and 6 months; discharge summary; in-house pharmacy can prepare a take-home supply). Shipping abroad and customs need owner.

researchQuestions.question: Are the herbal medicines made under GMP and tested for heavy metals?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Patients in Europe and the USA have read press reports about heavy metals in some Ayurvedic products. The FAQ's 'natural sources' line does not reassure them.

researchQuestions.question: I rely on coffee or cigarettes (or a drink in the evening). How will you help me through stopping, since abstinence is 'strictly adhered to'?

researchQuestions.answerSource: this page (the abstinence rule) and /faqs-downloads/ (campus is alcohol- and caffeine-free). Withdrawal support needs physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: What if the programme isn't helping, or I need to leave early? Is anything refunded?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The terms say 'Change in Date during Stay – No Refund'. A patient with anxiety needs to know there is a safe exit and what it costs.
researchQuestions.answerSource: this page (T&C) and /cancellation-and-refund-policy/. Clinical review and early-discharge policy need physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: Do I need a medical visa or an e-tourist visa, and will you send an invitation letter?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Required for every international patient, and the page is silent on it.
researchQuestions.answerSource: another site page: /faqs-downloads/ (Medical Visa or Medical Attendant Visa may be more appropriate; invitation letter on request) and /how-to-reach/

researchQuestions.question: How do I get there from the airport, how long is the drive, and is the transfer included?

researchQuestions.answerSource: another site page: /faqs-downloads/ (Coimbatore 75 km, about 2 h; Cochin and Calicut 125 km; transfers charged one way, book 48 h ahead) and /how-to-reach/ (named driver, late-night arrivals, wheelchair-accessible vehicle)

researchQuestions.question: Can my spouse, who is also stressed, do the programme too, or just stay with me, and what does that cost?

researchQuestions.question: Will my mental-health information be kept confidential?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: European and US patients expect privacy for psychiatric history, and they may disclose medication and diagnoses during pre-programme teleconsultation.
researchQuestions.answerSource: another site page: /privacy-policy/. Clinical-record handling needs owner.

researchQuestions.question: Can I stay reachable for work (Wi-Fi in the villa) or do a digital detox? Will I have quiet time away from groups?

researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (Wi-Fi in common areas; ask about in-villa) and this page (private yoga and meditation at extra cost). A digital-detox policy needs owner.

researchQuestions.question: Is there a best season for the stress programme?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Monsoon heat and humidity affect comfort and flight planning.
researchQuestions.answerSource: another site page: /faqs-downloads/ (summer, March–May, suits stress-management treatments; the physician advises)

researchQuestions.question: I have limited mobility. Can I manage the therapy tables, villa steps and campus paths?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Older patients with joint problems as well as stress need to know before booking.
researchQuestions.answerSource: another site page: /faqs-downloads/ (ramps, mobility assistance) and /how-to-reach/ (wheelchair-accessible vehicle, caregiver). Therapy-room access needs owner.

researchQuestions.whyItMatters: International patients plan how they will pay before they book.
researchQuestions.answerSource: another site page: /faqs-downloads/ (no cashless tie-ups; reimbursement documents provided; cards, bank transfer, cash in INR, EUR or USD)

title: Cardiovascular Health & Blood Pressure Treatment

faqs.question: Can I attend if my blood pressure is not well controlled?
faqs.draftAnswer: Ask your treating clinician about the suitability of travel and a residential stay. Share recent readings and your medicine list so the proposed programme can be discussed in the context of your existing care.
faqs.reviewRequired: Confirm admission thresholds, monitoring, escalation and medication responsibility.

faqs.question: How do I know whether this programme is suitable for me?
faqs.draftAnswer: Explain your diagnosis, current symptoms and goals before booking. In particular, discuss recent blood-pressure readings, heart or kidney disease and antihypertensive medicines. Ask whether this programme is appropriate and whether another form of care is needed first.
faqs.reviewRequired: Confirm eligibility, exclusions, reports required and how suitability is assessed before payment/travel.

faqs.question: Can I continue my prescribed medicines?
faqs.draftAnswer: Do not stop or change prescribed medicines on your own. Share a complete list of medicines and supplements with your treating clinicians and discuss any proposed Ayurvedic medicines with them.
faqs.reviewRequired: Confirm interaction review, prescribing responsibility, communication with existing clinicians and programme-specific restrictions.

faqs.question: What risks or side effects should I discuss before treatment?
faqs.draftAnswer: Ask the physician to explain the risks and alternatives for each proposed procedure or medicine in relation to your health. Raise any new symptoms promptly and ask what help is available if you become unwell.
faqs.reviewRequired: Provide specific common/serious risks, contraindications, monitoring, escalation and actual out-of-hours arrangements. Do not publish a zero-risk claim.

faqs.question: What results can I realistically expect, and how long should I stay?
faqs.draftAnswer: Results and suitable duration vary. Discuss achievable goals and how progress would be reviewed before booking. A stated minimum stay is a booking condition, not a promise of improvement within that time.
faqs.reviewRequired: Confirm programme-specific goals and duration; substantiate or remove existing outcome percentages and cure/permanence claims.

faqs.question: Can a companion stay with me?
faqs.draftAnswer: Non-participating companions are considered case by case. Tell the team about your accommodation and assistance needs before booking, and ask for confirmation of availability, responsibilities and charges.
faqs.reviewRequired: Owner-approved case-by-case principle from 7 September; business owner must confirm rates/inclusions, clinical team must confirm care duties and dependency limits.

faqs.question: What follow-up should I arrange after returning home?
faqs.draftAnswer: Before leaving, ask what advice you should take home, who to contact with questions and how ongoing care should be coordinated with your usual clinician. Confirm any follow-up appointments and charges before agreeing to them.
faqs.reviewRequired: Confirm actual discharge documentation, clinician availability, cadence, channel, charges and medicine supply/export arrangements.

researchQuestions.question: I take 2–3 blood-pressure tablets, often with a statin, aspirin or blood thinner. Will your physicians ask me to reduce or stop them? Who decides, and how do you stop my pressure dropping too low once herbs and therapies are added?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: This is the first safety question for any patient on antihypertensives, and it decides whether their own cardiologist or GP objects. The page contradicts itself: the FAQ says 'alongside conventional medications', while Benefits promise 'reducing reliance on synthetic medications'.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner. Dr. Deepu John must answer. The site's own FAQ ledger (faq-content-2026.json, 'Can I continue my current (allopathic) medicines during treatment?') is marked no-recorded-fact.

researchQuestions.question: I also have diabetes, high cholesterol, kidney disease, or a past heart attack, stent, stroke or atrial fibrillation. Am I eligible? Is there a blood-pressure level or heart condition at which you would not admit me?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: At 40–70, hypertension rarely comes alone. The title says 'Cardiovascular Health' and the hero 'heart health', which suggests cardiac patients are covered, but no eligibility or exclusion is stated.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner. The /faqs-downloads/ ledger items 'Which conditions do you NOT treat?' and 'Can I take Panchakarma if I have diabetes or high blood pressure?' are both unanswered, pending Dr. Deepu John.

researchQuestions.question: Are the heat and oil treatments safe with high blood pressure (herbal steam baths, Abhyangam, Shirodhara, Udwarthana)? Is my BP checked before each therapy, and what happens if it is high that morning?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Inclusions promise daily 'herbal steam baths' and the routine names Udwarthana. This generic copy is shared with other programmes, and a hypertensive reader worries about spikes.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner: therapy selection for hypertension and the pre-therapy BP-check protocol.

researchQuestions.question: What can I realistically expect by discharge after 14 nights, and how will it be measured (daily BP charting; lipids, kidney function and ECG at admission and discharge)? Will I get the readings in writing?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The FAQ says results take 'several months', the stay is 14–28 days, and the testimonial says BP 'returned to normal' by departure. The patient needs honest expectations and objective measures to justify a long-haul trip.
researchQuestions.answerSource: The expected outcome and monitoring protocol need physician/owner. /faqs-downloads/ ('Will I receive a discharge summary...') confirms admission and discharge notes, treatment summaries and prescriptions are provided.

researchQuestions.question: What will the total cost be? The rates are per night, but herbal medicines and lab tests are extra and 'can only be ascertained as your treatment progresses'. What is the typical range for this programme, and when do I pay it?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: A 100% advance plus an open-ended medicine bill contradicts 'All-Inclusive Pricing: No hidden fees!'. International patients budget in EUR/USD and need a ceiling.
researchQuestions.answerSource: The 14-night total (from ₹3,01,938, Deluxe single) is on /all-programs/ and could be shown here. The typical medicine and lab cost range needs physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: Who exactly will treat me (names, qualifications, experience)? Do they speak English, German, French, Russian or Arabic? Is a modern-medicine doctor or cardiologist available if needed?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: This page says only 'Ayurvedic doctor' and 'Doctor might change as subject to availability', and claims 'multilingual staff' without naming languages.
researchQuestions.answerSource: Qualifications are on /online-consultation/: Dr. Deepu John, Chief Physician & HOD, BAMS; Dr. Akhila Oommen, BAMS; Dr. Rahul R, BAMS. Languages need physician/owner (FAQ ledger: no-recorded-fact). Allopathic or cardiology cover needs physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: If I have a pressure spike, chest pain or stroke symptoms at night, who responds, and how far is the nearest hospital with a cardiac unit?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: This is the core fear of a hypertensive patient flying to rural Kerala, and the page does not address it.
researchQuestions.answerSource: Partly on /faqs-downloads/ ('arrangements with nearby hospitals and emergency services'; recommends travel insurance with evacuation cover). Night and weekend physician cover, and the named cardiac hospital with travel time, need physician/owner (ledger item 'Is a doctor available at night and on weekends?' is unanswered).

researchQuestions.question: Do I need a medical visa? Will you send an invitation letter? Do I get my 100% advance back if the visa is refused?

The refund on visa refusal needs physician/owner (ledger item 'Is the advance payment refundable if my visa is refused?' is unanswered).

researchQuestions.question: Is this a hospital or a holiday resort? The page says 'resort', 'Luxury Stay' and lists spa awards. Will my insurer, employer or visa officer accept it as medical treatment, and will I get invoices for reimbursement?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Both credibility and reimbursement depend on it. The page's hospitality wording undercuts the NABH message.

researchQuestions.question: How many nights do I need for my blood pressure (14, 21 or 28), and who decides?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page lists '14/21/28 days' with no criteria, and the cost triples between options.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ 'How long should I stay' (14 nights for most chronic-condition programmes; the physician confirms at consultation). Hypertension-specific criteria need physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: After I fly home, do I keep taking your herbal medicines? For how long, at what monthly cost? Can I carry them through customs? Are follow-up consultations included in the price?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The FAQ says results take 'several months' and Inclusions promise a 'Continuous post-discharge wellness plan', but the page never says what it contains or costs.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ says the in-house pharmacy prepares a take-home supply and online follow-ups are typically at 1, 3 and 6 months. Cost, whether it is included, and duration need physician/owner. Customs rules are country-specific and need owner guidance.

researchQuestions.question: Are your herbal medicines tested for heavy metals, and are they safe with my statin, aspirin or anticoagulant?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: European and US patients often read about heavy metals in Ayurvedic products, and their GP will ask about interactions before approving the trip.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /online-consultation/ mentions an in-house 'WHO-GMP-certified pharmacy'. The testing and drug-interaction policy needs physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: Is the food low-salt? Can it also suit my diabetic or kidney diet? Is it vegetarian only?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Salt restriction is central to BP control, and the diet FAQ is generic dosha language.
researchQuestions.answerSource: This page: vegetarian or vegan sattvic meals, three a day. Salt, renal and diabetic adaptations need physician/owner (kitchen).

researchQuestions.question: What does a hypertension patient's day actually look like: which two therapies, how long each, and how much rest?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The routine shown is a generic template with one therapy slot and Udwarthana. It does not match the Shirodhara, Thakradhara and Nasyam this page names, so the patient cannot picture the programme.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner: a programme-specific sample day.

researchQuestions.question: Can my spouse come without treatment? What does it cost, and can we share one villa? Does the 'Double' rate mean two patients?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Most 40–70 patients travel as a couple, and the tariff's Single/Double columns don't say who is treated.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/: extra bed ₹3,000 / $43 / €38 and extra meals ₹5,500 / $79 / €69 per night; two people can share a villa on different programmes. What the 'Double' rate covers needs physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: Which airport do I fly into, how long is the drive, and is the transfer included? The page lists 'Airport transfers' under Inclusions.
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: A long drive after a long-haul flight is a real concern for older hypertensive patients, and the page implies the transfer is free.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /how-to-reach/: Coimbatore CJB about 1½–2 h; Kochi COK about 2½–3 h; named driver. /faqs-downloads/: transfers are paid, e.g. Coimbatore ₹6,775 MPV one way.

researchQuestions.question: I'm 68 with stiff knees. Are there steps? Are there ramps and grab rails in the villa bathroom? How far is the treatment block? Can I have a wheelchair at the airport?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Mobility limits are common in this age group, and the page says nothing about accessibility.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ senior-patient answer (ramps, mobility assistance). /how-to-reach/ (wheelchair-accessible vehicle and caregiver on request). Villa-level specifics need physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: Which reports should I send before the free consultation: ECG, echo, lipid profile, kidney function, a week of home BP readings?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page says only 'recent reports', and a well-prepared consultation is what converts an enquiry into an admission.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /online-consultation/ (the first consultation is free; reports are optional). The programme-specific report list needs physician/owner (ledger item 'Should I send my medical reports before I come?' is unanswered).

researchQuestions.question: If it isn't helping or I feel unwell, can I leave early and get anything back?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: 'What if it does not work' is a key booking blocker under a 100% advance with no-refund terms.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /cancellation-and-refund-policy/: no refund for the unused portion on early departure; exceptional cases subject to management approval. Medical-reason exceptions need physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: Will female patients be treated by female therapists (and men by men)? What privacy is there during oil treatments?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: This is decisive for Middle East patients and important to many European women. Nothing on the site states the policy (only an image caption shows a female therapist).
