researchQuestions.question: How do I pay from abroad: card in EUR/USD, or bank transfer? Can I pay from Russia?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: 100% advance is required, and some patients' banks or cards are restricted.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/: Visa/Mastercard/Amex, bank transfer, cash in INR/EUR/USD; the rates are also quoted in USD and EUR on this page. A Russia-specific payment channel needs physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: When is the best season for a blood-pressure programme? Isn't Kerala very hot?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Heat and humidity worry older hypertensive patients planning dates.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ best-time answer (general seasonal guidance). Hypertension-specific timing needs physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: Is a long-haul flight safe for me with high blood pressure, and should I arrive a day early to rest?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Fitness to fly is a common worry before a 10+ hour trip.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner (plus the patient's own doctor)

researchQuestions.question: I drink 3 coffees a day and I smoke. Coffee and smoking are banned; will withdrawal headaches or BP changes be managed?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page states strict abstinence but not how the transition is handled, which matters for a BP patient.
researchQuestions.answerSource: This page (abstinence from smoking, alcohol and coffee). Management needs physician/owner.

existingClinicalFlags: FAQ answer 'Ayurvedic treatment can be used alongside conventional medications for hypertension.' This is a blanket safety statement. The site's own FAQ ledger marks the allopathic-medicine policy as unconfirmed, pending Dr. Deepu John. It needs his wording on continuing, adjusting and monitoring antihypertensives, including hypotension risk.

Medication-replacement messaging that could lead patients to stop BP medicines: 'Ayurvedic therapies and herbal medicines provide natural alternatives, reducing reliance on synthetic drugs and their potential side effects'; Benefits 'reducing reliance on synthetic medications'; audience line 'Individuals with hypertension seeking natural alternatives'; testimonial heading 'Regaining Control Naturally'.

Cure framing in the FAQ: the question 'Can Ayurvedic treatment completely cure hypertension?' and the answer 'a complete cure depends on various factors and individual responses', which implies cure is possible for some. Also 'Ayurveda offers long-term solutions to manage and control blood pressure levels effectively.'

Outcome timeline in the FAQ: 'some clients experience improvements within a few weeks... several months of consistent treatment'. The physician must confirm or replace it, and reconcile it with the 14/21/28-day stay.

Efficacy claims in Benefits and Process: 'Balances blood pressure, reduces stress, and enhances cardiovascular health'; 'Improves circulation, supports healthy cholesterol'; 'Strengthens the immune system and addresses root causes of hypertension'; 'Customized herbal formulations will be prescribed to support cardiovascular health, regulate blood pressure, and reduce inflammation'; 'Custom herbal remedies support cardiovascular health and regulate blood pressure'.

Toxin and lasting-result claims: 'Ayurvedic procedures, herbal products, and massages ... eliminate toxins and restore health'; 'Ayurveda addresses hypertension at its roots, promoting lasting well-being and improved heart health'; 'Trust our expertise for holistic, effective hypertension management'; 'Ongoing support ensures long-term health'.

Patient testimonial as outcome evidence: 'by the time I left, my blood pressure had notably returned to normal' (Ms. Shalu, 5.0 stars). The owner must verify its provenance and consent. The physician must approve its use for a medical condition, with a 'results vary; not a substitute for your prescribed treatment' disclaimer. The 'Transformative Results' label also needs sign-off.

Therapy suitability for hypertensive patients. The generic inclusions promise 'Two Ayurvedic therapies per day, including herbal steam baths'; the routine names Udwarthana and 'a warm herbal bath'; the programme names Shirodhara, Thakradhara, Abhyangam and Nasyam. The physician must confirm which of these are used, adapted or excluded for hypertension (especially sudation/steam), and whether BP is checked before each therapy.

Yoga and pranayama in the routine ('Practice yoga asanas (postures) for 30-45 minutes to stimulate the body'; daily group yoga; pranayama). The physician or yoga lead must confirm these are adapted for hypertensive patients (e.g. inversions, breath retention) before this generic schedule is shown on a BP page.
Doctrinal statement 'addresses hypertension as a dosha imbalance, primarily in Pitta and Vata doshas', and Nasyam claimed to 'improve circulation'. The physician must confirm accuracy.

Scope implied by 'Cardiovascular Health' in the title and 'heart health' in the hero and meta. The physician must define which cardiovascular conditions the programme accepts and which it excludes (e.g. coronary disease, heart failure, arrhythmia, recent stroke), or narrow the naming to blood pressure.

Programme length '14/21/28 days' and the tariff's 'Minimum Duration is 14 Nights' for hypertension. The site-wide FAQ (signed off by Dr. Deepu John) says chronic-condition programmes run 'from 7 to 14 nights depending on the condition'. The physician must confirm the hypertension minimum and the criteria for 21 or 28 nights.

Whether this programme includes any Panchakarma: Nasyam is listed as a treatment, while 'specialty therapies (e.g., Panchakarma)' are billed as add-ons. The physician must state what is clinically included.

Related-programme links. If the page is reworked to link hypertension to stress, diabetes or weight-management programmes (instead of spine care), the physician should confirm those pairings are clinically appropriate.

title: Neurological Wellness & Function Therapy

faqs.question: Which neurological conditions does the programme cover?
faqs.draftAnswer: Provide your diagnosis and the support you currently need. Ask whether the programme is appropriate for that condition and how it would fit with neurological and rehabilitation care.
faqs.reviewRequired: List accepted diagnoses and exclusions, functional assessments, rehab services and referral pathways.

faqs.question: How do I know whether this programme is suitable for me?
faqs.draftAnswer: Explain your diagnosis, current symptoms and goals before booking. In particular, discuss neurological diagnosis, seizure history and daily assistance needs. Ask whether this programme is appropriate and whether another form of care is needed first.
faqs.reviewRequired: Confirm eligibility, exclusions, reports required and how suitability is assessed before payment/travel.

faqs.question: Can I continue my prescribed medicines?
faqs.draftAnswer: Do not stop or change prescribed medicines on your own. Share a complete list of medicines and supplements with your treating clinicians and discuss any proposed Ayurvedic medicines with them.
faqs.reviewRequired: Confirm interaction review, prescribing responsibility, communication with existing clinicians and programme-specific restrictions.

faqs.question: What risks or side effects should I discuss before treatment?
faqs.draftAnswer: Ask the physician to explain the risks and alternatives for each proposed procedure or medicine in relation to your health. Raise any new symptoms promptly and ask what help is available if you become unwell.
faqs.reviewRequired: Provide specific common/serious risks, contraindications, monitoring, escalation and actual out-of-hours arrangements. Do not publish a zero-risk claim.

faqs.question: What results can I realistically expect, and how long should I stay?
faqs.draftAnswer: Results and suitable duration vary. Discuss achievable goals and how progress would be reviewed before booking. A stated minimum stay is a booking condition, not a promise of improvement within that time.
faqs.reviewRequired: Confirm programme-specific goals and duration; substantiate or remove existing outcome percentages and cure/permanence claims.

faqs.question: Can a companion stay with me?
faqs.draftAnswer: Non-participating companions are considered case by case. Tell the team about your accommodation and assistance needs before booking, and ask for confirmation of availability, responsibilities and charges.
faqs.reviewRequired: Owner-approved case-by-case principle from 7 September; business owner must confirm rates/inclusions, clinical team must confirm care duties and dependency limits.

faqs.question: What follow-up should I arrange after returning home?
faqs.draftAnswer: Before leaving, ask what advice you should take home, who to contact with questions and how ongoing care should be coordinated with your usual clinician. Confirm any follow-up appointments and charges before agreeing to them.
faqs.reviewRequired: Confirm actual discharge documentation, clinician availability, cadence, channel, charges and medicine supply/export arrangements.

researchQuestions.question: Do you treat my specific diagnosis (Parkinson's, multiple sclerosis, diabetic or peripheral neuropathy, post-stroke weakness, Bell's palsy, early dementia, epilepsy), and which conditions do you decline?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page says only "nervous disability" and "nervous system imbalances". Nobody flies from Europe or the Gulf without knowing their disease is in scope.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner. Related pages: /treatment-for-paralysis/ and /treatment-for-facial-paralysis/ cover subsets. /online-consultation/ promises the physician will say plainly if a programme is not appropriate.

researchQuestions.question: Can I keep taking my neurological medicines (levodopa, anti-epileptics, MS disease-modifying therapy, blood thinners, antidepressants), and will anyone tell me to stop them?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: This is the top safety fear for neuro patients and their neurologists. FAQ 3 dodges it with "ensuring compatibility".
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner (Dr. Deepu John)

researchQuestions.question: Do the herbal-mineral medicines (bhasma/rasaushadhi) contain heavy metals? Are they tested, and can I get an ingredient list to show my neurologist?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Western patients have read about heavy metals in Ayurvedic preparations. FAQ 2's "natural herbs and minerals" raises the worry instead of settling it.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner. /online-consultation/ mentions the group's WHO-GMP pharmacy, but no testing or ingredient-disclosure fact is stated.

researchQuestions.question: What result can I realistically expect, and by when: symptom relief, slower progression, or possibly nothing for a progressive disease? What happens if it does not help?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page promises "lasting results" and "transformative results" with no timeframe or honest limits. Older patients with chronic neuro disease distrust that.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner. /online-consultation/ has usable honest-limits wording ("sometimes that view is that our programmes are not appropriate").

researchQuestions.question: How many nights do I need for a neurological condition, and is 7 nights enough?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page gives only "Villas — Minimum Duration is 7 Nights". Sister pages differ: /treatment-for-paralysis/ says 14 nights minimum and 14–28 days typical. International flights make this a key planning fact.
researchQuestions.answerSource: another page (/faqs-downloads/ says neurological chronic-condition support runs "7 to 14 nights depending on the condition"). The recommended length for this programme needs physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: I am 68 with heart disease, diabetes and high blood pressure alongside my neurological condition. Am I medically suitable, and are therapies like Shirodhara, Nasyam or Pizhichil safe for me?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Comorbidities are the norm at 40–70. Nothing on the page addresses age or co-existing conditions.
researchQuestions.answerSource: another page (/faqs-downloads/: no stated maximum age, "Modified treatments suitable for senior patients"). Individual suitability and contraindications need physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: Who will treat me (name, qualifications, neurological experience), and do they speak English, German, French, Russian or Arabic?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page says "Our specialists" and "multilingual staff" but names nobody and no languages. It even warns "Doctor might change".
researchQuestions.answerSource: another page (/online-consultation/: Chief Physician Dr. Deepu John, BAMS; /faqs-downloads/: BAMS-qualified physicians). Languages spoken and any neuro specialisation need physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: I have poor balance or use a wheelchair or walker. Are the villa, bathroom and treatment rooms accessible, and how do you prevent falls on oiled treatment tables and floors?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Mobility impairment is common in this group. Oil therapies (Pizhichil, Abhyanga) are a real slip risk.
researchQuestions.answerSource: another page (/how-to-reach/: wheelchair-accessible vehicle and caregiver on request; /faqs-downloads/: ramps, mobility assistance). Villa-level accessibility and fall precautions need physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: What happens if I have a seizure, a fall or stroke symptoms during my stay? Is a doctor on campus at night, and which emergency hospital is nearest and how far?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Neuro patients and their families need an emergency plan before booking a remote rural campus.
researchQuestions.answerSource: another page (/faqs-downloads/: "arrangements with nearby hospitals and emergency services", "Emergency medical services on call"). The named hospital, distance and night cover need physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: What will my treatment days actually be, meaning which of Shirodhara, Shirovasti, Nasyam, Pizhichil and Pichu, how often and for how long?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The only sample day shown is generic: Udwarthana "detox", 30–45 minute yoga, nature walks. It does not match a neuro programme or a patient with limited mobility.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner

researchQuestions.question: Which reports should I send before booking (MRI, nerve conduction study, neurologist letter, medication list), and will a physician review them before I pay?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Patients want an expert to see their records before paying 100% in advance for a long-haul trip.
researchQuestions.answerSource: another page (/online-consultation/: free pre-consultation with an optional reports form). The neuro-specific report list needs physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: Is there physiotherapy or rehabilitation exercise, or only yoga and massage-type therapies?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Patients coming from Western neuro care expect rehabilitation. The page mentions only yoga, meditation and oil therapies.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner

researchQuestions.question: What is the realistic total cost for a neuro programme once medicines, lab tests and extra therapies are added?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page says "All-Inclusive Pricing: No hidden fees!", then says medicines and tests "will cost extra" and can only be ascertained as treatment progresses. That is the classic trust-breaker.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner (typical range). Villa rates on this page: ₹21,567–₹48,267 single per night.

researchQuestions.question: Can my spouse or a caregiver stay in the villa and help me, and what does it cost?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Many neuro patients cannot travel alone.
researchQuestions.answerSource: this page (Addons: extra bed ₹3,000 / $43 / €38, meals ₹5,500 / $79 / €69) and another page (/faqs-downloads/: a family member can stay; /how-to-reach/: caregiver can be arranged for the transfer)

researchQuestions.question: Is the airport transfer included, and which airport should I fly to?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: This page lists "Airport transfers" under Inclusions, while another page prices them separately.
researchQuestions.answerSource: another page (/how-to-reach/: Coimbatore CJB nearest, Kochi COK alternative, named driver; /faqs-downloads/: transfer from ₹6,775 MPV one way from Coimbatore)

researchQuestions.question: Do I need a medical visa, and will you provide an invitation letter?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Required planning for patients from Europe, the Middle East, the USA and Russia. Not mentioned on this page.
researchQuestions.answerSource: another page (/faqs-downloads/: Medical Visa or Medical Attendant Visa may be appropriate; invitation letter on request; /how-to-reach/: Government of India visa portal)

researchQuestions.question: Will my health insurance reimburse this, and what documents will I get?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: International patients over 40 usually check reimbursement first.
researchQuestions.answerSource: another page (/faqs-downloads/: no cashless tie-ups; invoices, treatment summaries, prescriptions and admission/discharge notes provided for reimbursement)

researchQuestions.question: If the physician finds on arrival that I am not suitable, or I have to leave early because of my condition, do I lose my 100% advance?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page requires 100% advance payment and "No Refund" inside 15 days. /cancellation-and-refund-policy/ gives no refund for early departure. That is scary for someone with an unpredictable neurological condition.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner (a medical-unsuitability or illness exception is not stated anywhere)

researchQuestions.question: What follow-up do I get at home, can a report go to my neurologist, and can I legally import the herbal medicines into my country?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Chronic neuro conditions need continuity. "Ongoing support" and "Continuous post-discharge wellness plan" are vague.
researchQuestions.answerSource: another page (/faqs-downloads/: online follow-ups typically at 1, 3 and 6 months; discharge notes and treatment summary for your home doctor). Medicine shipping and customs need physician/owner.

researchQuestions.question: Is this a real hospital or a luxury spa holiday? The awards on the page say "Spa Resort" and "Luxury".
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: A neuro patient, or their neurologist, will dismiss a "spa" on sight. Half the page is hospitality award badges.
researchQuestions.answerSource: this page (NABH accreditation AH-2024-0250 for Panchakarma) and another page (/online-consultation/: "a medical institution, not a leisure property")

researchQuestions.question: Is the Kerala heat or monsoon a problem for my condition (e.g. heat sensitivity in MS), and when is the best time to come?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Heat intolerance is common in MS and some neuropathies, and it affects when patients book.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner

researchQuestions.question: Can the kitchen handle swallowing difficulty (dysphagia), diabetic needs or other restrictions alongside the prescribed Ayurvedic diet?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Dysphagia is common in Parkinson's and after a stroke. The page promises only "tailored" vegetarian or vegan meals.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner

researchQuestions.question: Will I have to give up coffee straight away, and what if I get withdrawal headaches?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page states "Abstinence from Smoking, Alcohol, & Coffee is strictly adhered to" with no guidance. Headaches worry neuro patients.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner

existingClinicalFlags: FAQ 1: "Yes, Ayurvedic treatment … can help alleviate nervous disabilities". An unqualified efficacy "Yes" across all neurological conditions.
FAQ 2: "Yes … made from natural herbs and minerals, minimizing the risk of adverse effects". An unqualified safety claim; the mineral preparations are not addressed.
FAQ 3: "ensuring compatibility and safety" when combined with other medicines. A guarantee, with no instruction not to stop prescribed neuro medication.
About: "an Ayurvedic Program for Nerve Regeneration". The page claims nerve regeneration.
About: "Ayurveda … offers an effective approach to addressing these issues", said of neurological disorders.
About: neurological disorders are "often caused by imbalanced Vata dosha". A causal claim that needs the physician's framing as Ayurvedic understanding.
About: "Ayurvedic diagnostics provide accurate insights".
Approach: "Customized medications from natural herbs and minerals aim to restore balance and strengthen the nervous system", and "lasting results".
Who it's for: "natural remedies for cognitive impairments" and "long-lasting results for nervous system health". This implies dementia or cognitive-decline benefit.
Why opt: "enhance cognitive function, and strengthen the nervous system for lasting well-being" and "prioritizing safety and effectiveness by blending Ayurvedic wisdom with modern expertise".
Why opt: "Our specialists focus on nervous disability treatment". Is there a neuro-specialised physician to back this?
Benefits list stated as outcomes: "reduced symptoms of stress and anxiety", "Improved cognitive function", "Strengthened nervous system resilience, restored balance, and increased vitality".
Post Treatment: "Ongoing support ensures long-term health", and "Continuous post-discharge wellness plan". Guarantee language.

Testimonials: the "Transformative Results" heading plus the single unverified testimonial "My time at Kairali changed my life … I was physically and mentally stronger" about a "neurological disease". Needs verification, consent and outcome-claim review.

Therapy list (Shirodhara, Shirovasti, Nasyam, Pizhichil, Pichu, Abhyanga) given as treatment for neurological disorders with no indications or contraindications, e.g. in epilepsy, uncontrolled hypertension or recent stroke.

Generic day plan offered for neuro patients: Udwarthana "to promote detoxification", 30–45 minute yoga asanas, nature walks, and a "detoxifying drink to kickstart the metabolism". Suitability for patients with mobility or balance impairment and the detox or metabolism claims need sign-off.
"Personalized Diet" / "Three organic, sattvic meals": any claimed therapeutic effect of the diet on neurological conditions needs sign-off before it is expanded.

researchQuestions.question: Is it safe to take your herbal medicines and have oil therapies while I am on chemotherapy, immunotherapy, targeted therapy or hormone therapy (e.g. tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitors)? Will they interact with my cancer drugs?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Herb–drug interaction is the first thing an oncologist asks and the most common reason patients do not book. The page promises "herbal formulations" and "immune system strengthening" but never mentions interactions.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner (Dr. Deepu John): which herbs are avoided with which drug classes and how interactions are screened

researchQuestions.question: Should I stop or delay any of my oncology treatment to come?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: FAQ 2 says the programme is not a replacement, but no answer says "never stop or delay oncology treatment". A patient deciding on a 14-night minimum stay needs that said plainly.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /disclaimer/ §6 already says patients should maintain all ongoing treatment and follow their own physicians' advice; confirm cancer-specific wording with the physician

researchQuestions.question: Do you need my oncologist's written approval, and which reports must I send before booking (latest blood counts, staging, scans, treatment summary, drug list)?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page only says "Bring: ... recent reports & open mind". Patients having chemotherapy need to know whether they will be accepted before paying 100% in advance.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner (the free online consultation on /online-consultation/ may be where reports are reviewed; confirm)

researchQuestions.question: Who is NOT suitable: low blood counts, metastatic disease, recent surgery, a port/PICC line, lymphoedema, bone metastases, radiotherapy skin reactions?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: "Who is this programme for" lists only two lines and no exclusions. Massage, heat, steam baths and purgation all carry specific risks for these patients.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner

researchQuestions.question: When in my treatment should I come: between cycles, after the last cycle, how long after surgery or radiotherapy? Can the 14-night minimum fit between chemotherapy cycles?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page targets people "undergoing chemotherapy" but requires "Minimum Duration is 14 Nights", which usually clashes with a 2–3-week cycle.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner (the 14-night minimum is on this page; timing and exceptions need the physician)

researchQuestions.question: Which therapies will I actually receive: Panchakarma purgation, Abhyanga, Shirodhara, Udwarthana, herbal steam? Are they changed for cancer patients?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The daily routine is generic, e.g. "Udwarthana ... to promote detoxification" and a warm herbal bath. Patients with neuropathy, fatigue or fragile skin need to know the therapies are adapted.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner

researchQuestions.question: What happens if I get a fever, infection or other complication during my stay? Which hospital with oncology or emergency care is nearest, how far is it, and is a doctor on site at night?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Neutropenic fever is a medical emergency for chemotherapy patients far from their own oncology team.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ says there are "arrangements with nearby hospitals and emergency services" and recommends evacuation insurance; the hospital name, distance and night cover need owner

researchQuestions.question: Is it safe for an immunocompromised patient to take part in group yoga, the pool, the organic farm visit and the soil/composting class?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The weekly schedule includes a farm visit and a class on "Soil health and composting". Soil and shared-water exposure is an infection risk during chemotherapy, and infection control is not mentioned.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner (infection-control policy, which activities are physician-cleared)

researchQuestions.question: Does the physician have experience with cancer patients? Will they talk to my oncologist and give me notes to take home?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Patients aged 40–70 trust their oncologist first and need to know the Ayurvedic physician will work with them, not against them.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /online-consultation/ names Dr. Deepu John (Chief Physician, BAMS), Dr. Akhila Oommen and Dr. Rahul R; /faqs-downloads/ confirms discharge notes and treatment summaries for your home doctor; oncology experience needs physician/owner

researchQuestions.question: What can I realistically expect to improve (fatigue, appetite, nausea, sleep, neuropathy, mood), how soon, and how is progress measured?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The page offers "Transformative Results" but no condition-specific, honest expectations. Overpromising here is both a trust risk and a clinical risk.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs physician/owner (no outcome may be invented; /disclaimer/ §7 already states no results are guaranteed)

researchQuestions.question: Is this price per villa or per person, what will 14 nights cost in total, and roughly how much should I budget for medicines and blood tests?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The tariff shows per-night figures without a basis. The page says "All-Inclusive" yet lists medicines, lab tests and Panchakarma as extras, which may be a large part of the cost for this condition.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs owner (rate basis and a typical medicine/lab cost range)

researchQuestions.question: If my oncologist postpones my cycle or I am too unwell to fly, do I lose my 100% advance?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Cancer schedules change often. The page requires 100% advance and gives no refund under 15 days, with nothing about medical postponement.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs owner (medical-postponement policy); the general policy is on /cancellation-and-refund-policy/ and /faqs-downloads/

researchQuestions.question: Are airport transfers included, and how far is the hospital from the airport?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: This page lists airport transfers under Inclusions, but /faqs-downloads/ says they cost extra. The two pages also disagree on distance: Coimbatore is 75 km on /faqs-downloads/ and ~62 km on /how-to-reach/; Kochi is 125 km vs ~115 km.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /how-to-reach/ and /faqs-downloads/ (transfer prices); owner must reconcile the distances and the inclusion

researchQuestions.question: Which visa do I need for supportive cancer care: tourist, e-Medical, Medical Attendant for my spouse? Will you send an invitation letter?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Patients from Russia, the Middle East, Europe and the USA need this before booking flights, and a companion needs its own visa type.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (Medical Visa / Medical Attendant Visa, invitation letter on request) and /how-to-reach/; the current rules are on the Government of India visa portal

researchQuestions.question: Can my spouse or carer stay with me, what does it cost, and can they also have treatment?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Most patients having chemotherapy will not travel alone, and a carer's cost changes the decision.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (extra bed ₹3,000 / $43 / €38 and extra meals ₹5,500 / $79 / €69 per night); whether the carer can have treatment needs owner

researchQuestions.question: I am 68 with diabetes and heart disease as well as cancer. Can I still come?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Patients aged 40–70 often have comorbidities; the page says nothing about age or other conditions.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (no stated maximum age); comorbidity suitability needs physician

researchQuestions.question: Is the vegetarian sattvic diet enough if I am losing weight or have mouth sores or taste changes? Can it be made soft, high-protein or diabetic?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Nutrition is a top worry during chemotherapy. The page's "lean protein sources" line is confusing for a vegetarian kitchen.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /ayurvedic-cuisine/ and /faqs-downloads/ (organic vegetarian meals); adaptations for cancer patients need physician

researchQuestions.question: The routine starts at 06:00 with 30–45 minutes of yoga and a nature walk. Can I rest if I am exhausted, and are sessions optional?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Cancer-related fatigue is common. The page says the day plan "may vary" but does not say that rest is allowed.
researchQuestions.answerSource: partly on this page ("The above day plan is a general outline and may vary..."); the intensity policy for cancer patients needs physician

researchQuestions.question: Is the campus step-free and wheelchair-accessible (villas, therapy rooms, dining hall), and how far are the walks between buildings?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Patients with weakness, neuropathy or low blood counts may not manage long walks or stairs.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /how-to-reach/ (wheelchair-accessible vehicle and accompanying caregiver can be arranged); on-campus accessibility needs owner

researchQuestions.question: In which languages can I speak with the doctor? Is an interpreter available for German, French, Russian or Arabic?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Discussing cancer symptoms and medicines through a language barrier is unsafe. The page says only "multilingual staff".
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs owner (languages actually spoken by physicians and staff); /how-to-reach/ says only that English is widely spoken

researchQuestions.question: Is this a hospital or a wellness resort? Are there nurses and doctors on site every day and at night?

researchQuestions.answerSource: this page (NABH certificate AH-2024-0250) and /faqs-downloads/ (NABH-accredited hospital, BAMS physicians); staffing and night cover need owner

researchQuestions.question: Can I keep taking the herbal medicines at home, will customs in my country allow them, and are they tested for heavy metals?

researchQuestions.question: Will my health insurance pay for any of it, and what documents will I get?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: It decides affordability for many European and Gulf patients.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (invoices, treatment summaries, admission/discharge notes for reimbursement; approval depends on the insurer)

researchQuestions.question: Is emotional or psychological support available (counselling, not only meditation)?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: About says "Cancer patients’ physical and mental problems are addressed", but only group meditation and yoga are described.
researchQuestions.answerSource: needs owner/physician

researchQuestions.question: Is a long-haul flight safe for me (blood-clot risk, low blood counts), and which season is best in Palakkad?

researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (seasonal temperatures); flight fitness is for the patient's own oncologist, to be said plainly on the page

existingClinicalFlags: Title, H1, meta and OG framing: "Ayurvedic Cancer Recovery & Strengthening Program" and "Boost immunity, reduce side effects & regain strength with Kairali’s Ayurvedic cancer recovery program". This implies recovery from cancer and states outcomes.
FAQ 2: "...lowering symptoms, managing side effects, and promoting a full recovery." This implies full recovery from cancer.

FAQ 1: "boosting immunity, minimizing side effects". FAQ 3: "immune system strengthening, stress reduction, energy enhancement, and detoxification". These are immunity and detox claims to cancer patients, including those on immunotherapy.
FAQ 4: treatments tailored to "cancer types". This implies cancer-type-specific protocols. The physician must confirm which cancer types and treatment stages are accepted or excluded.

About: "Cancer patients’ physical and mental problems are addressed by these treatments", "enhancing immunity, reviving vitality" and "has a long history of offering comprehensive care" for cancer patients. Efficacy and track-record claims.
Who it is for: "Patients undergoing chemotherapy for cancer". Whether residential therapy during active chemotherapy is suitable, and on what clearance, needs physician sign-off.
Process step 04: "Panchakarma, a comprehensive detoxification process, helps eliminate toxins from the body", presented as standard for these patients.

Why choose / Benefits: "By strengthening the immune system, it reduces the risk of illnesses", "It focuses on preventing health issues before they arise", "prevents potential health issues" and "supporting long-term wellness and longevity". Longevity implies survival benefit.
"Transformative Results" H2 over three generic Panchakarma testimonials on a cancer page. Implies outcomes this programme may not deliver.

Daily routine and inclusions given to chemotherapy patients without adaptation: "Udwarthana (herbal powder massage), to promote detoxification", "herbal steam baths", "a warm herbal bath", "detoxifying drink to kickstart the metabolism", 30–45 min yoga asanas, daily group yoga, nature walks. Intensity and suitability need sign-off.
Organic farm visit and the "Soil health and composting" agriculture class, offered with no infection-control note to possibly immunocompromised patients.
Sunday session: "practical do’s and don’ts to maintain optimal health and prevent diseases naturally". A disease-prevention claim.
During Treatment: "continued doctor support for a safe and effective journey". A safety and efficacy promise.
Follow-up: "The practitioner may suggest herbal supplements" and "Continuous post-discharge wellness plan". Herbal medicines continued at home alongside oncology drugs need an interaction statement.

Missing safety statement: the page never tells patients to keep their oncology treatment, or that herbs are screened against their cancer drugs. /disclaimer/ §6 has general wording; a cancer-specific version needs physician sign-off.
Classical programme name "Karkaroga Sahayam Chikitsa": the physician should confirm the correct term and spelling (Karkataroga?).

title: Spinal Disc & Nerve Restoration Treatment

faqs.question: Can I join with a slipped disc or nerve symptoms?
faqs.draftAnswer: Share your diagnosis, imaging reports if available and any specialist advice. Ask whether the proposed programme fits your condition; do not delay assessment of new or worsening neurological symptoms.

existingClinicalFlags: Hero, meta and og description: "Heal slip disc naturally … Restore spine health" promises healing and restoration of a structural disc lesion.
The programme name "Spinal Disc & Nerve Restoration Treatment" and the Sanskrit name "Snayu Bala Chikitsa" imply nerve repair. Physician to confirm both names are clinically accurate.

Recurrence and cure claims: "not only heals your spine comprehensively but also rejuvenates it, reducing the chances of recurrence"; "heal the slip disc, relieve pain, and prevent recurrence"; "prevent slip disc recurrence"; "Our approach ensures long-term relief, prevention".
Tissue and disc regeneration: "promote tissue regeneration" (Approach, Process step 05, FAQ 2) and "nourish spinal discs".

"a successful track record of treating 30,000+ slip disc patients" and "proven track record in slip disc treatment": unsourced patient volume and success claim. Scope and evidence are needed from the owner, or remove.

Medication and surgery-avoidance messaging: "reducing the need for pain medications" and "avoid or minimize the use of pain medications and invasive procedures". This needs physician wording plus a red-flag statement (bladder/bowel change, saddle numbness, progressive weakness or foot drop means urgent medical assessment, not this programme).

FAQ 3 safety claim "generally safe as it utilizes natural therapies and herbal medications": the physician must state contraindications and how herbal medicines are checked against existing prescriptions.
"Our ancient Ayurvedic treatments … provide stability and firmness to the affected area" and "offer a tangible solution to spine problems" are efficacy claims.

The therapy protocol differs across sections (Elakizhi/Vasti/Kativasti vs Abhyanga/Pizhichil/Kati Basti/Greeva Basti). The physician must approve one list and say whether "Vasti" (Panchakarma enema) is part of this programme.

The generic day plan includes Udwarthana (herbal powder massage) "to promote detoxification", 30–45 min yoga asanas at 06:30, daily group yoga and a nature walk. The physician must confirm suitability for acute disc or nerve pain, or state that activity is prescribed per patient.
"Ayurveda … views slip disc as a Vata dosha imbalance affecting movement and the nervous system": this traditional framing needs physician approval.
The FAQ 1 definition of a slip disc is imprecise and states symptoms as certain. Physician to approve a corrected definition.

A testimonial-based outcome claim (Mrs. Ashu: "regain the flexibility I had feared I had permanently lost") sits under the heading "Transformative Results". It needs patient consent on file, and the owner and legal must check whether outcome testimonials are permitted in Ayurvedic treatment advertising.
The promise of "Daily Consultation" with a physician (package icons) vs "Daily wellness check-ins": owner and physician to confirm what is actually delivered daily.

existingClinicalFlags: FAQ 1: "Ayurvedic treatment has been proven effective in managing arthritis by reducing pain, and inflammation, and improving joint mobility." This is an absolute efficacy claim with no evidence.

FAQ 2: "Ayurvedic therapies and medications are generally safe… We prioritize the use of natural herbs to minimize side effects." This safety statement conflicts with Process step 05, which says the medicines are made from "natural herbs and minerals". The physician must confirm how mineral-containing formulations are selected and monitored.
FAQ 3: "Typically, noticeable improvements can be observed within a few weeks". An outcome timeline for OA and RA needs physician wording.

FAQ 4: "Ayurvedic treatment can be integrated with conventional medicine." This needs an explicit physician policy for DMARDs, biologics, corticosteroids, NSAIDs and anticoagulants, including a line never to stop prescribed medicines without the prescribing doctor.
Benefits: "reduces medication reliance" is effectively stop-medication advice for RA and OA patients.
Who For: "Individuals who prefer natural therapies and medications over conventional treatments" may lead RA patients to abandon DMARDs.
Who For: "treat the underlying causes of the issue rather than just the symptoms" claims root-cause resolution for degenerative and autoimmune disease.

About: "If you’re experiencing joint pain, fever, fatigue, and loss of appetite, it could be Arthritis" encourages self-diagnosis. Fever with joint pain needs urgent medical assessment (possible infection).
About: "immune system strengthening" is presented as an aim for a programme that includes rheumatoid arthritis, which is autoimmune.

About: "For Rheumatoid Arthritis, a body cleansing plan is employed along with therapies like Elakizhi, Pizhichil" is a stated treatment protocol. The physician must confirm it and say whether the cleansing is chargeable Panchakarma.

Subtitle "Sandhivātam Chikitsa… { Osteo & Rheumatoid }": in classical usage Sandhivata generally corresponds to osteoarthritis, while RA is usually described as Amavata. The physician must confirm the Sanskrit label.

Hero/meta: "Reduce joint pain, inflammation & improve mobility" and Benefits "Reduced pain, inflammation, and stiffness while enhancing joint mobility… Improved overall quality of life" state outcomes as certain.
Our Approach: "Trust in our expertise for lasting relief and improved vitality" promises a lasting outcome.

Process step 02: diagnosis by "pulse examination (Nadi Pariksha) and visual examination (Darshana Pariksha)… identify the root cause". The physician should state what lab or imaging review applies for arthritis.

"aids in healing and restoring your pelvic structure, promoting healthy lactation, reducing stress, and relieving neck and backaches". Structural and lactation outcome claims.

Benefits list: "Speeds postpartum recovery, reduces fatigue, and balances hormones"; "Aids in pain relief, boosts emotional well-being, and improves sleep"; "Enhances immunity, supports weight management".
"restoring your strength, energy, and shape" and "regain your pre-pregnancy vitality". Body-shape and weight outcome claims.
"Holistic post-pregnancy care addresses physical, emotional, and mental well-being". This implies the programme treats postpartum mood disorders; it needs a scope statement and a referral pathway.

Naming the programme "Sutika Paricharya" and grounding it in the "Sutika Kala" regimen, while admission starts only after that period ends. The physician must define what the programme is clinically.

The day plan shown: detox drinks "to kickstart the metabolism", Udwarthana "to promote detoxification", 30–45 minutes of asanas at 06:30, and pool and gym access. Is each suitable for lactating and post-caesarean mothers?
History copy: "strengthening the uterus" and "gentle detox therapies" presented as the programme's basis.
"Personalized Herbal Formulations ... address specific post-pregnancy issues". Which formulations, and are they safe while breastfeeding?
"Ongoing support ensures long-term health". A guaranteed-outcome claim.

The testimonial under "Transformative Results" (Mrs. Ankita: "My energy level increased thanks to the food advice and herbal supplements"). The outcome claim needs review, and the patient's consent to publication needs confirming.

researchQuestions.question: Will my skin get worse before it gets better? Can the detox or oil therapies trigger a flare, and what happens if they do?

The physician must confirm which are admitted to this 14-night inpatient programme, which go to Psoriasis & Chronic Skin Treatment, and which are declined.

Benefit and outcome promises: 'reduced inflammation and redness ... clearer, healthier complexion', 'your skin gains fortified natural defense mechanisms', 'strengthening immunity—leading to luminous, resilient skin', 'restore the natural glow, elasticity, and health of the skin'.

'prepare herbal medicines following Ayurvedic principles for purity and effectiveness' is a purity and effectiveness claim. Confirm the quality-testing basis (e.g. heavy metals) before publishing.

The day-plan therapy examples (Udwarthana dry herbal powder massage, herbal steam baths, oil pulling, warm herbal bath) are generic, not skin-specific. The physician should confirm they suit inflamed, broken or sensitive skin (eczema, rosacea, sunburn) or replace them with skin-appropriate examples.

Mechanism framing: 'Ayurveda identifies skin ailments as dosha imbalances', 'removing toxins (Ama) ... treat the underlying causes', 'internal imbalances—often the root cause of skin issues'. These are acceptable only as traditional-theory framing in physician-approved wording, not as established biomedical cause.

Benefits list: 'restored facial symmetry', 'enhanced nerve function' and 'long-lasting results' promise outcomes.
FAQ 1: 'addressing the root cause… leading to long-lasting results' implies the programme is better than conventional care.

FAQ 3: 'natural and typically do not cause significant side effects' is a safety claim. It contradicts /faqs-downloads/ Q15 and ignores herb–drug interactions (Ashwagandha, Brahmi and Bala are named on the page).
FAQ 4: 'several weeks to a few months for noticeable improvement' states a recovery timeframe, and it conflicts with the 14/21/28-day programme.
Programme length '14/21/28 days' is presented as the treatment course, but the rates source states only a 14-night minimum.

The 'Who is This Program For?' list includes stroke-induced palsy, parotid gland disorders, postoperative palsy and traumatic nerve injury, with no exclusion or referral criteria. For example, parotid tumours and progressive or unexplained palsy need investigation first, and a patient in the acute stroke window needs a neurologist first.

The page has no red-flag or referral statement: sudden facial weakness can be a stroke and needs emergency care, and Ayurvedic care should not replace or delay standard early treatment of Bell's palsy. Dr. Deepu John must approve the wording.
Eye protection during Nasyam, Shirodhara, Ksheeradhoomam and oil therapies for incomplete eye closure is not addressed.

Cause, dosha and symptom statements need correction: 'nerve occlusion', 'imbalances in the Vata and Pitta doshas' vs 'aggravated Vata', and 'numbness… speech difficulties' and 'reduce facial swelling'.
'Medicinal herbs such as Ashwagandha, Brahmi, and Bala, along with Rasayanas, strengthen the nervous system' is an efficacy claim for named herbs.
'Our experienced doctors specialize in neurology' is a qualification claim the roster does not support (BAMS only). The same sentence is on /treatment-for-paralysis/.
The testimonial outcome claim ('my facial movement improved… restoration of face muscle control') needs the patient's provenance and consent confirmed, plus a physician-approved results-vary note.
The generic day plan (Udwarthana, 'detoxifying drink', 'promote detoxification') shown on a facial-paralysis page needs the physician to confirm what is actually prescribed for this condition.

existingClinicalFlags: 'Our experienced doctors specialize in neurology': credential claim. The site's stated credentials are BAMS (Dr. Deepu John, Chief Physician; Dr. Akhila Oommen).
'Our therapies and natural remedies stimulate nerve regeneration, reduce inflammation, and promote recovery': mechanism and outcome claim.
'Specific herbal formulations and Rasayana therapies are used to regenerate nerve tissues': tissue-regeneration claim.
'Ayurveda addresses the root cause of paralysis for lasting results': root-cause and permanence claim (for stroke the cause is vascular).
Benefits list: 'Improved muscle strength and control, enhanced nerve function', 'restored symmetry', 'long-lasting results': outcome promises.
'Shirodhara … improves neurological function': outcome claim.
Hero, meta description and og:description: 'Improve mobility & nerve function with holistic healing', plus the programme name 'Paralysis Recovery …': implied outcome.

Testimonial 'My limbs’ strength and sensibility were restored', headed 'Transformative Results' and 'Success Stories': outcome claim through a single, first-name-only testimonial. Needs verification, consent and a results-vary statement.

FAQ 1 labels Abhyangam, Pizhichil and Kizhi as 'Panchakarma treatments', and says they 'enhance muscle strength, nerve function, and overall mobility': wrong classification and outcome claim. The same text is emitted in the FAQPage JSON-LD.

Process step 02 prescribes Virechana (purging) and Swedana, and calls it 'essential for recovery': purging in elderly post-stroke patients on antihypertensives or diuretics is a safety matter the physician must approve. Swedana is misclassified as Panchakarma. Basti/Nasya are not mentioned; the physician should confirm the actual protocol.
FAQ 2: 'Paralysis, according to Ayurveda, is caused by an imbalance in Vata dosha': causal wording should be framed by the physician as Ayurvedic classification, not medical causation.
FAQ 3: 'typically 14 to 28 days or more' and 'promote maximum recovery and long-term benefits': duration and outcome claim.
Process step 06: diet 'focused on boosting nerve health and immunity' and 'prevent further complications': prevention claim that stroke patients will read as preventing recurrence.

'Who is This Program For?' eligibility list (Bell's palsy, nerve compression, postoperative paralysis, traumatic nerve injury), with no contraindications or timing after an acute stroke: the physician must set inclusion/exclusion criteria and say when after a stroke admission is appropriate.

'Yoga and Physiotherapy … Gentle physiotherapy exercises' and 'combining ancient Ayurvedic therapies with modern techniques': the physician/owner must confirm physiotherapy is actually delivered and by whom.
Generic Dinacharya timetable on a paralysis page (yoga asanas 30–45 min, nature walk, oil pulling, Udwarthana): the physician should confirm or replace it for hemiplegic patients.

Safety content that is missing but needed on this page: burn risk from hot Kizhi/Pizhichil/steam on limbs with sensory loss, handling of the hemiplegic shoulder, fall risk after oil therapies, and herb interactions with anticoagulants. Any answer written for these needs Dr. Deepu John's sign-off.

researchQuestions.question: Is the airport transfer included, and which airport should I fly to?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: This page lists 'Airport transfers' under Inclusions, while /faqs-downloads/ prices them as an extra cost. That surprises a patient at the point of booking.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /how-to-reach/ and /faqs-downloads/ (transfer fares). Note that the two pages give different airport distances (CJB 62 km vs 75 km). The owner must confirm included vs chargeable.

researchQuestions.question: Can my husband or wife come with me, and what does it cost? Does 'Double' mean two patients or a patient plus a companion?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Most 40–70 patients travel with a partner. The tariff shows Single/Double per night without saying whether both people are treated.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ ('Can a family member stay with me…': extra bed/meals). What the Double rate covers needs the owner.

researchQuestions.question: What happens after I go home — can I get my medicines abroad or through customs, and is online follow-up included?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Psoriasis needs long-term maintenance. Patients worry about running out of medicines, customs rules in the EU/US/Russia, and whether follow-up is free.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ ('How do I continue my Ayurvedic routine after returning home?': online follow-ups, medicines for purchase). Cost, frequency and shipping/customs need the owner.

researchQuestions.question: Are your medicines safe? Do they contain heavy metals or bhasmas, and where are they made?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Heavy-metal content in some Ayurvedic preparations is a common Western concern, and many dermatologists raise it with patients.
researchQuestions.answerSource: Needs physician/owner: the source and manufacturing standard of the formulations dispensed at KTAHV (not stated on this page).

researchQuestions.question: Should I book the Psoriasis programme or the Skin Vitality Revival programme?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: /treatment-for-skin-diseases/ also lists 'Eczema and psoriasis' and carries a psoriasis testimonial. Two overlapping pages with no stated difference split the decision and search intent, and neither links to the other.
researchQuestions.answerSource: Needs owner/physician to define the difference. Both pages exist in the prerender set.

researchQuestions.question: Will insurance pay for this?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: European and US patients expect a claim route. Knowing there is none, or only reimbursement, changes the budget.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ ('Are Ayurvedic treatments covered by insurance?': no cashless tie-ups; treatment summaries and medical certificates provided for reimbursement claims).

researchQuestions.question: What will I eat, and can you handle diabetic or gluten-free needs? Is dairy really excluded?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: The FAQ says 'avoiding dairy, red meat' while using buttermilk (Takradhara) and serving an all-vegetarian kitchen. A patient with comorbidities needs a clear, consistent answer.
researchQuestions.answerSource: Needs physician for the psoriasis diet. The vegetarian-only rule is on /cancellation-and-refund-policy/ and /faqs-downloads/.

researchQuestions.question: When is the best season to come for psoriasis — monsoon humidity or dry winter?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: International patients plan months ahead, and the climate affects psoriatic skin.
researchQuestions.answerSource: The general seasonal guide is on /faqs-downloads/ ('When is the best time to visit for specific treatments?'). A psoriasis-specific recommendation needs the physician.

researchQuestions.question: I have limited mobility or knee/joint pain (psoriatic arthritis). Are the villas and therapy rooms step-free?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Patients over 60 with psoriatic arthritis may not manage steps or getting on and off a treatment table.
researchQuestions.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (ramps, mobility assistance) and /how-to-reach/ (wheelchair-accessible vehicle). Villa-level step-free access needs the owner.

researchQuestions.question: Can I use the pool and shared areas with visible plaques, and is psoriasis a problem for other patients?
researchQuestions.whyItMatters: Visible psoriasis carries stigma. Patients worry about being stared at or excluded, and whether oiled skin and the pool mix.
researchQuestions.answerSource: Needs physician/owner.

existingClinicalFlags: 'The actual reason behind Psoriasis is yet to be known but it is said to be hereditary in nature.' This describes the cause of the disease and needs physician wording.

'The underlined reason can be considered to be the increase of pitta dosha in the body.' This gives a dosha cause for psoriasis. Classical texts treat Kushtha as tridoshic, and psoriasis is often correlated with Ekakushtha/Kitibha (vata-kapha).

'…has come up with a new and exceptional solution to your skin problems', together with 'Has it shown results even after going through courses of different types of medicines?', implies superiority over conventional treatment.
Benefits: 'Enhances skin health and decreases symptoms like scaling and itching'. This is a symptom-outcome claim.
'Improves vitality and strengthens the immune system' and 'Improved immunity and overall vitality' claim an immune-boosting effect in an immune-mediated disease.
'Balance restoration and prevention of further complications' and 'Prevents health issues by addressing the core cause' are prevention/root-cause claims.
FAQ 1: 14–28 days with 'For best results, the doctors may suggest a lengthier stay'. This needs a physician-set duration and must not imply outcomes.

FAQ 2: the named protocol (Abhyanga, Takradhara, medicated herbal baths, internal medicines, Panchakarma as needed). The physician must confirm the actual psoriasis protocol, and whether Udwarthana (hero image, sample day) is used on psoriatic skin.
FAQ 3: the diet rules ('excludes inflammatory items', 'avoiding dairy, red meat', diet 'based on their body composition'). This contradicts Takradhara (buttermilk) and needs physician correction.
FAQ 4 and 'Continuous post-discharge wellness plan': what home care, herbal remedies and follow-up are actually provided.
'Panchakarma, a comprehensive detoxification process, helps eliminate toxins from the body' (Process step 04).
'…continued doctor support for a safe and effective journey'. This is a safety and efficacy claim.

The indications list 'Patients with hormonal skin conditions' / 'Individuals with complex skin disorders', with no contraindications stated. The physician should define who is suitable and who is not (e.g. erythrodermic/pustular flares, pregnancy, patients on biologics).

The patient testimonial ('My skin felt calmer and less inflamed…', 'genuinely life-changing') under the heading 'Transformative Results'. This is an outcome claim for disease treatment; the owner must verify the testimonial's source and it needs physician/regulatory review before use.
The Sunday session 'prevent diseases naturally' and the 'Detoxifying Drink… kickstart the metabolism' lines. These are generic health claims repeated on a condition page.

Missing entirely: any statement on existing psoriasis medication (methotrexate, biologics, steroids) — whether to continue it or how to taper. This is the page's highest-risk gap and needs Dr. Deepu John's wording before it can be added.
